required_actions: Connect the USB drive to the PC (critical)
Select File Explorer from the taskbar and open the folder with the photos or videos (critical)
Select the files, then select Cut on the ribbon (critical)
Open the USB drive and select Paste (critical)
Settings route: Start, Settings, System, Power & battery, expand Energy saver, set Always use energy saver to On (critical for this turn)
Restart: Start, Power, Restart, as a second try (page: under Other things you can do)
Power troubleshooter: Settings, System, Troubleshoot, Other troubleshooters, Run next to Power (page: under Change power settings)
reasons: Borderline, kept: the page gives the restart as a fix for problems that shorten battery life, not for Energy saver failing to switch on. The reply does not claim it fixes the toggle, so it is not counted as a source failure. Data Lead may want the fallback reworded.

unsupported_claims: 'If it does not, a USB Bluetooth adapter can add it.' -> neither the pairing page nor the 'Fix Bluetooth problems in Windows' page mentions USB Bluetooth adapters or dongles. The fix page only says 'Some devices don't have Bluetooth' and to check the product specifications for Bluetooth capabilities.
reasons: G1: the USB adapter suggestion is not on either official page. Everything else in the troubleshooting steps is supported by the second page (Bluetooth devices discovery, Advanced).
fix: In the last paragraph, replace 'If it does not, a USB Bluetooth adapter can add it.' with 'If it does not, check the product specifications to make sure it has Bluetooth capabilities.' Keep everything else. Page support for the new sentence: 'Some devices don't have Bluetooth' and 'check the product specifications to make sure it has Bluetooth capabilities' (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/bluetooth/fix-bluetooth-problems-in-windows).

required_actions: Press Windows key + Plus sign (+) to turn Magnifier on (critical)
Press Windows key + Plus sign (+) again to zoom in (critical)

required_actions: Press Windows key + Plus sign (+) to turn Magnifier on, if it is not on (critical)
Press Ctrl + Alt + L to switch to Lens view (critical)
Press Ctrl + Alt + F to switch back to Full screen view (critical)
reasons: S5: 'To go back to the whole screen' uses a phrase that is not the page's label, and it can suggest that Ctrl + Alt + F turns magnification off. The page names this view 'Full screen view' (Ctrl+Alt+F). The shortcuts are supported by the second source (keyboard-shortcuts-for-magnifier).
fix: Replace 'To go back to the whole screen, press Ctrl + Alt + F.' with 'To switch back to Full screen view, press Ctrl + Alt + F.' Keep the rest.

Follow the consent prompt to process voice on the device (critical)
Let Windows download the language files if asked
Check the default output device in Settings, System, Sound (page: default sound output device configured in Settings > System > Sound) (critical)

unsupported_claims: 'If it is not the headset you are using, change the default output device to your headset.' -> the cited page (use-live-captions) says only 'You might need to change your default device for audio to be picked up by live captions' and gives no steps for changing it. The how-to is on a different official page (see fix).
reasons: G1: the change step has no steps on the cited page. The location (Settings > System > Sound) and the need to change the device are on the page. The how-to is supported by the 'Fix sound or audio problems in Windows' page, which should be added as a second source. S4: step 3 bundles a check and a conditional change into one step.
fix: Keep steps 1 and 2 and the sentence 'Captions only show sound that goes to your default sound output.' Replace step 3 with two steps: '3. Under Output, check which device is selected.' and '4. If it is not your headset, select your headset in the Output section. Selecting it also makes it the default.' Renumber the last step as 5: 'Play the video again and check that captions show.' Add second source https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/audio/fix-sound-or-audio-problems-in-windows (page: Start > Settings > System > Sound; in the Output section choose the device; 'When you select this device, you're also setting it as the default.').
